summary.oneLiner: Piccadily Agro crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26 driven by premium IMFL brands, with a strategic demerger of the low-margin sugar business to focus purely on high-growth spirits. Guidance for 60-70% growth in FY27 is underpinned by the full monetization of new 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh capacity and resolved supply constraints at the Indri plant.

one-line thesis: Piccadily Agro crossed INR 1,000 Cr revenue in FY26 driven by premium IMFL brands, with a strategic demerger of the low-margin sugar business to focus purely on high-growth spirits. Guidance for 60-70% growth in FY27 is underpinned by the full monetization of new 200 KLPD Chhattisgarh capacity and resolved supply constraints at the Indri plant.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR 364 Cr (Q4, +33% YoY), INR 1,143 Cr (FY26, +28% YoY); EBITDA Margin: 23.4% (FY26, flat YoY), Q4 impacted by seasonal sugar margin compression (2% vs 11% prior); PAT: INR 46 Cr (Q4, +14% YoY), INR 140 Cr (FY26, +33% YoY); Order Book: N/A (FMCG); Net Debt: Short-term borrowings up 132% due to working capital for INR 100 Cr malt inventory buildup and receivables (DSO 80-90 days).
guidance: Revenue Growth: 60-70% in FY27 (Value driven); Margin: EBITDA % stable to +50 bps (absolute EBITDA up 60-70%); Order Inflow: Robust demand exceeding current capacity; Capex/Commissioning: Chhattisgarh (200 KLPD) fully commissioned Dec '25, monetizing from May '26; Indri expansion (220 KLPD total) complete Oct '25.
order book & pipeline: N/A for FMCG; Demand visibility strong with supply constraints now resolved; Malt inventory built up to INR 100 Cr to support future bottling.
segment / subsidiary detail: Alco-Bev Revenue: INR 908 Cr FY26 (+42% YoY); IMFL Brand Portfolio: INR 250 Cr Q4 (+67% YoY); Sugar Business: Margins compressed to 2% in Q4; Channel Mix: CSD/Paramilitary 30%, Exports 25%, Domestic Retail/HORECA 45%.
growth verticals / optionality: Chhattisgarh plant to contribute INR 300-400 Cr in FY27; Indri plant expansion to add INR 250-300 Cr; New product pipeline (premium/luxury extensions) kicking in Q1 FY27; Target to become top 5 global single malt brand in 3-5 years; Exports target 50% of revenue in 3-5 years.
margins & cost dynamics: IMFL EBITDA margins ~45-50%; Overall Alco-Bev EBITDA ~31.5%; Q4 margin dip due to sugar seasonality and temporary commodity cost inflation (husk/nakku); Packaging inflation (glass) currently absorbed via vendor contracts, potential pass-through if sustained.
capex / expansion: FY27 Capex guidance: INR 25-30 Cr (mainly for barrel expansion from 85k to 100k, warehousing, minor bottling tweaks); Major greenfield/brownfield capex completed.
capital allocation: Demerger of sugar business to unlock value and focus capital on Alco-Bev; Inorganic M&A under exploration for brand portfolio (domestic/international); Scotland distillery project in early stages (land/licenses secured).
risks & watch-items: Execution risk on 60-70% growth guidance; Regulatory changes in state excise policies; Input cost volatility (grain, glass, fuel); Competition in INR 4,000-5,000 single malt segment; High working capital cycle (DSO 80-90 days).
management quality / tone: Highly confident, aggressive on growth targets, transparent about one-off margin pressures, strategic focus on global branding and pure-play spirits exposure.
non-obvious takeaways: Company does not sell bulk malt despite capacity increase; all malt is reserved for own premium bottling; Scotland distillery project is in works but not yet operational; Auditor change is partner-led continuity (Krishnan Mangwa moving to new firm) rather than governance issue.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Supply constraints limited volume growth in FY26; new capacity now online | Piccadily Agro Industries Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of 450 KLPD total capacity and demerger clarity; FY27 guidance implies significant re-rating if executed. |

themes.title: Alco-bev premiumization
themes.need: Alco-bev players ride premium-&-above mix shift, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics - a pricing-power thesis distinct from staple rural-recovery/GST pull.
themes.driver: Premium-mix up-trading, single-malt/gin launches and state-excise/route-to-market dynamics.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- Describes itself as "India's largest independent producer of malt spirits", with a portfolio spanning single malt whisky, cane juice rum, vodka and IMFL brands, plus Ethanol, ENA, DDGS and white crystal sugar.
- Indri is claimed as the "top selling Indian Single Malt globally and India" and "Largest selling Single Malt in India, for two consecutive years" (2024, 2025), and "amongst top 15 Single Malts globally".
- Awards are presented as the validation mechanism: 191 total awards won since 2022 (Indri 139, Camikara 41, Cashmir 8, Whistler 3), including 50 awards in Q1 and "Best Indian Distillery of the Year" at the Tokyo Whisky & Spirits Competition 2026.
- Product-level moat claims: Indri's triple wood maturation and Himalayan terroir at Indri, Haryana ("a profile no competitor replicates"); Camikara as "India's First Pure Cane Juice Rum" (cane juice, not molasses); Cashmir distilled from Sona Moti, a revived 2,000-year-old heirloom Indian wheat.
- First to introduce the Indian Malt Whisky Association (IMWA) certification hologram on its bottles, positioned as an authenticity/credibility marker for Indian single malt.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Demerger] "Scheme of arrangement for Sugar business was filed with the Stock Exchanges on 28.4.2026 and is work in progress" — implying a separation of the sugar vertical from the distillery business.
- [Certification] First to introduce the IMWA certification hologram on Indri Single Malt bottles, certifying adherence to IMWA production standards and category integrity.
- [ESOP] Employee benefits expense includes an ESOP charge of Rs. 2.47 Cr for the quarter.
- [Market opportunity] Deck cites (S&P Global market intelligence / IWSR-based management estimates, 9-litre cases) India Spirits 420 Mn (2025) to 560 Mn (2030F) at ~6% CAGR; Indian Single Malt 0.53 Mn to 0.78 Mn at ~8%; Aged Premium Rum 34K to 77K at ~18%; Vodka 0.55 Mn to 0.97 Mn at ~12%.
- [Channel] CSD and Paramilitary institutional channels remain a stated focus for branded products, alongside 16 Indian and 19 international duty free outlets.
